summary: Phase 149O.20L.7H -- DeploymentBinding Producer Contract Independent Verification. Verification-only -- no implementation, no DeploymentBinding created, no repository identity created, no Dell mutation, no HBDC contract text amended. Independently reconstructed and adversarially verified 149O.20L.7G's HBDC-001 v1.1 amendment (section 16.1, HBDC-REQ-056..070, CBD-9/CBD-10) against primary source (git diff between the immutable pre-7G baseline 01a47f05 and post-7G commit 0b530959, src/pcae/core/hatp_bootstrap.py, src/pcae/core/repository_identity.py, the HMIC-001 contract text, and the CHGR governance record) rather than trusting 7G's own report as an oracle. Confirmed the exact contract diff (version 1.0 -> 1.1, exactly 15 new requirements added, CBD-9/CBD-10 added, zero existing requirement text altered, zero src/pcae/** files touched). Independently re-verified requirement-ID integrity (70 unique, gapless, each traced exactly once in section 24 -- an initial naive whole-document grep produced a false-positive duplicate from an unrelated table format in section 22, corrected by scoping to section 24 specifically). Built a full per-requirement verification matrix for all 15 new requirements (producer responsibility, inputs, validation rule, state mutation, failure behavior, authority dependency, audit requirement, consumer relationship, implementation surface). Ran a completeness/adversarial-contract attack constructing five candidate loopholes; found none that both are textually compliant and route around HBDC-REQ-066's admin-OS-principal-only invocation boundary, which remains the load-bearing security control in every examined path -- verdict: no Blocking completeness finding. Independently reproduced (not accepted from 7G) the F3-residual finding by direct reading of HMIC-REQ-103's 12-step validation algorithm: it never consults a live DeploymentBinding's status field, so a revoked binding does not invalidate an already-issued certification under current HMIC-001 text -- real, non-blocking, correctly out of HBDC-001's own scope, ownership assigned to a future HMIC-001 amendment. Independently reproduced the timestamp permissive-parser gap with a concrete Python repro (hatp_bootstrap.py's read-path parser accepts non-Z UTC offsets, >6-digit fractional seconds, and space-separated date/time forms that HBDC-REQ-067's strict grammar rejects) and assessed it as bounded by trust-store filesystem protection, not a trust-boundary bypass, since exploiting it requires the same maximal write access the legitimate admin writer itself requires. Performed a real git-worktree A/B regression test (not git stash, since 7G is already committed, merged history) on an independently grep-selected 17-file targeted subset: pre-7G 64 failed/713 passed/9 errors, post-7G 80 failed/697 passed/9 errors -- exactly 16 new failures, every one individually inspected by name and confirmed to be a historical HBDC-001 v1.0 byte/version-pinning assertion (version-string pins, original-55-requirement-shape pins, digest-mutation fixtures baselined on v1.0 bytes, whole-repo no-drift-since-phase-entry checks), none referencing src/pcae/**, Permission Broker, or live Dell state -- zero unexplained regressions in the sampled subset. Named eight new non-blocking clarification findings beyond what 7G identified: HBDC-REQ-059's idempotency-comparison field-set ambiguity (whether valid_from participates), HBDC-REQ-058's silence on cross-validating signer_key_id/provider_profile against existing trust-store vocabulary, HBDC-REQ-060/061's underspecification of rotate/revoke against a nonexistent entry, HBDC-REQ-062's silence on audit-write-ordering relative to trust-store-write success, HBDC-REQ-057's fail-closed-on-absent-identity rule living in architecture-doc prose rather than the frozen RFC-2119 contract text, the preview-architecture step being 'SHOULD' in prose rather than a numbered 'SHALL', and the absence of a concurrency-lock requirement analogous to the sibling HMIC-001 contract's HMIC-REQ-097 dedicated-lock discipline. Confirmed Dell's last-verified deployed source SHA (28bf137b, from 149O.20L.7E) is an ancestor of even the pre-7G baseline and 46 commits behind current HEAD -- Dell remains stale, no redeployment performed. Final verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- IMPLEMENTATION-READY. New independent 72-test companion module (does not import or trust the 7G companion module as an oracle), all 72 passing.
